In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inelastic scattering by ionized donors is a major relaxation mechanism in heavily doped n-GaAs/AlAs QWs.
the probability of scattering by neutral donors decreases with increasing temperature, while the probability of scattering due to electron-electron collisions increases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that inelastic scattering of hot carriers is important in the energy relaxation process in doped semiconductor structures.
inelastic scattering by ionized impurities dominates over other scattering mechanisms for the momentum relaxation of hot carriers in n-type GaAlAs quantum wells in the temperature range 10–80 K.
we have demonstrated the existence of a new channel of energy relaxation of hot electrons, namely, inelastic electron–donor collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the probability of hot electron scattering on neutral donors is comparable to the probability of scattering on neutral acceptors, and the probability of scattering by neutral donors can be comparable to the probability for scattering by charged impurities.

the probability of scattering by neutral donors in GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells decreases with increasing temperature, which can be used to explain a number of phenomena observed in experiments on the energy relaxation of hot electrons.
the probability of scattering by neutral donors in n-type GaAlAs quantum wells can exceed the probability of scattering in bulk semiconductors by an order of magnitude.
